title: fix(qa): check-platform-checklist judges `retired` by its own rule, not the active one
body:
Fixes #22987
Clause-②: no — a repository gate script; no published schema, accept set or public surface is touched

Unblocks #22869: PR #22982 (the retire of `records-forms.picklist-org-append`) lands after this PR. #22869 remains open until PR #22982 lands.

## The rule added

`scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs#statusFieldProblems` had one branch, for `planned`. Every other status, `retired` included, fell through to the active rule (`since` a release, `steps` non-empty). So a planned item retired before it was implemented had no legal shape: `since: null` and no steps is exactly what the README's Retire step (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/README.md`, Lifecycle) leaves it with.

The new `retired` branch follows that Retire step, and it returns early the way the `planned` branch does, so the active rule now covers `active` and `draft` only:

- `retiredReason` must be a non-empty string. Refusal: `a retired item must carry "retiredReason" as a non-empty string`.
- `since` must be `null` or release-shaped (`RELEASE_RE` reused). The refusal names both legal spellings and says only the SHAPE is checked, because this ledger holds no release timeline.
- `steps` is not judged. Absent, empty, or the steps the item ran with while active all pass. No selector runs a retired item: `scripts/checklist-select.mjs` builds its runnable pool from `status === 'active'` and its planned pool from `'planned'`.
- `supersededBy` is not read here. The existing referential pass after the walk still checks that it lands on a real id.

The planned and active rules are unchanged; F1–F16 are untouched and green. No new required field.

**Change from the card's premise:** the item walk already refused a retired item that had no `retiredReason`, using its own message outside `statusFieldProblems`. Adding the rule to the branch while keeping that check would report the problem twice, and the self-test can only drive the pure function. So the check moved into the branch, and the walk now only skips the acceptance requirement for retired items. As a side effect, the rule now sits behind the `statusFieldProblems(item)` call site that G1/G3 already pin.

**Battery:** R1–R12 go into the existing status battery (`selfTestPlannedStatus`), and its floor rises from 42 to 54. I did not add a new battery function, because a new compound-named self-test function needs a row in `COMPOUND_ANCHOR_LEDGER` in `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs`, which this card keeps frozen.

## Readings (this repo; base `712361b7a`, final head `1901eba70`)

`pnpm check:platform-checklist`, verdict line of the tree step:

- base `712361b7a`, ledger as on main, unfixed checker: `check-platform-checklist: 8 problem(s)`
- unfixed checker (`712361b7a`) with PR #22982's `records-forms.json` + `coverage.json` applied, uncommitted: `check-platform-checklist: 10 problem(s)`. The two extra lines are both on `records-forms.picklist-org-append`: the active rule's `"since" must be the release that introduced the capability…` and `"steps" must be a non-empty array of strings`.
- fixed checker (`1901eba70`), ledger as on main: `check-platform-checklist: 8 problem(s)`. Diffed line for line, these are the same 8 lines as base.
- fixed checker (`1901eba70`) with PR #22982's two ledger files applied, uncommitted: `check-platform-checklist: 8 problem(s)`. Same 8 lines as base; no line names `picklist-org-append`.

The 8 are the open main-red symbol-anchor set (#22924: `access-security`, `attachments-storage`, `search`), and this PR does not touch it. I applied PR #22982's files with `git restore --source` from a worktree-private ref at `57ef232b7`; main has not touched `docs/qa/platform-checklist/` since that PR's merge-base `117817ec2`, so the files carry exactly that PR's delta. I restored them with `git checkout HEAD --`. Restore proof, both times: `git diff HEAD` is empty, `git status --porcelain` is empty, and `git hash-object` equals the HEAD blob for both files (`707de16a36d7…`, `542fd62c23ce…`). No ledger file is committed here.

Self-test:

- `712361b7a`: `✓ check-platform-checklist --self-test: 221 assertions — …`
- `1901eba70`: `✓ check-platform-checklist --self-test: 233 assertions — …`. `✓ checklist-select self-test: 31 cases pass.` runs ahead of it.

**Ablation** (on the committed fix at `ce66b832d`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`): anchor `if (item.status === 'retired') {` replaced by `if (false && item.status === 'retired') {`. On disk the anchor went x1 to x0 and the marker x0 to x1; blob `6064a9e249a9` became `2469abeb42c0`, then was restored to `6064a9e249a9`, equal to HEAD, with `git diff HEAD` empty. Reading:

```
✗ check-platform-checklist --self-test — 10 failure(s)
```

R1 and R3–R11 go red. R2 and R12 stay green because the active rule accepts both. The G-rows (the call-site text pin that the header above `statusBindingProblems` describes) also stay green under this mutation. G12 already discloses this: a dead branch is a semantic severing that a text pin cannot see. What holds the branch is the new fixture rows, and the floor comment says so.

## Gates (final head `1901eba70`)

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, run from the worktree with no paths, derives 30 commands. All 30 were run at `1901eba70`, each with its exit code recorded. Reconciliation:

```
✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 30 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 30 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 30 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).
```

29 exit 0. `pnpm check:platform-checklist` exits 1, and that is the base 8 above. Selected verdict lines:

- `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`: `✓ dispatch-gates self-test (fast tier): 1828 cases pass; 6 slow section(s) deferred.` (exit 0)
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes`: `check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 10999 text file(s) -- 10999 tracked, 0 untracked-not-ignored; skipped 9 binary; no raw ASCII control bytes).`
- `pnpm check:entry-guard`: `✓ check:entry-guard: 285 scripts/ file(s) — every entry guard goes through invoked-as.mjs; …`
- `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`: `✓ comment-mask corpus sweep [scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs]: 8836 files, 0 disagree, 0 unparseable, …`

The script's own tests, beyond the derived families: no `scripts/**/*.test.*` or `scripts/__tests__/**` file names it (the pathspec matches 2 files, with 0 hits). The watchdog does not import this script; it only names the path as a string. I ran it anyway: `OK check-platform-checklist-watchdog self-test: 42 assertions across 8 floored batteries, …`.

Lint (narrowed to the one touched file; CI runs the full `pnpm lint`): `eslint --no-inline-config --format json scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` checks 1 file with 0 errors and 0 warnings. `--print-config` shows the effective config applies 2 rules (`no-restricted-imports`, `comment-swallow/no-code-inside-block-comment`), with parserOptions `ecmaVersion: latest, sourceType: module` and no `parserOptions.project`. Type-aware linting is not enabled anywhere in `eslint.config.mjs`, so this diff cannot change any untouched file's verdict.

Changeset: none; this PR carries `skip-changeset`. The root package is private, and no package manifest ships `scripts/`.

## Acceptance notes

- The active rule's refusal `"steps" must be a non-empty array of strings` names a string check that does not exist: only array-ness and length are checked. That is the kind of advertising this function's docblock forbids. Left alone because the card keeps the active rule frozen. This is a read-only inference, not filed.
- The dispatch assumed that the header-described mutation battery would go red when the new branch is dropped. Measured, it does not (text pin, G12). The new R-rows go red instead; see the ablation above.
- The card read `origin/main` at `246edf5b3`; this branch is cut from `712361b7a`. The base reading of 8 problems is the same on both.
